case: Raynham Hall Brown Lady photograph 1936 — Indre Shira

voice.name: Stephen S
voice.note: mature English male, London accent, deep — a 1930s professional photographer

segments.r_open: You have seen my photograph. Most people have. [pause] I was there, at the foot of the staircase, when she came down it.
segments.r_s1: A job. Country Life sent us — me and Captain Provand — to photograph a country house in Norfolk. Furniture. Panelling. Staircases. [soft laugh] The dullest work in photography. We had done the staircase once already. Provand had his head under the black cloth, setting up a second plate. I was behind him, looking up the stairs.
segments.r_s2: A vapoury form — gradually taking the appearance of a woman. Those are my words from the time. I have never found better ones. She was coming down the stairs, towards us. Not walking, quite. Descending. [pause] I shouted. Provand couldn't see a thing — his head was still under the cloth. The cap came off the lens, the flash fired. And she was gone.
segments.r_s3: He thought I had lost my mind. [soft laugh] He had seen nothing, and he said there could be nothing on that plate but a staircase. I told him there would be. We were still arguing in the darkroom when the negative came up. [pause] And there she was. On the stairs. Exactly where I had watched her come down.
segments.r_s4: Everyone said we faked it. So Harry Price came — the man who spent his life catching fraudulent mediums. He questioned the two of us, and he examined the negative, and his verdict was printed: I could not shake their story, and I had no right to disbelieve them. The negative, he wrote, is entirely innocent of any faking. [pause] The house had a name for her long before we came. The Brown Lady. She had been seen on those stairs for a hundred years.
segments.r_s5: Country Life printed her that Christmas, and she has never stopped being printed. People have had a lifetime to prove a trick — double exposure, grease on the lens, a fault of light. Let them try. [pause] Provand never claimed to see her. He was under the cloth, and he said so plainly all his life — that is an honest man. I did see her. I saw her before the flash, not after. [pause] It is the most famous photograph of a ghost in the world. I only pressed the trigger. Make of it what you like.

small: The witness is a professional photographer.

yt_title: Raynham Hall: You Have Seen My Photograph
